# Parent-drift breadcrumb comment (echo-safe, nearest-represented-ancestor)

## Context / Problem

When a local parent cannot be represented in Jira — the parent is a non-epic and this
project permits only Epic parents — the outbound differ already **suppresses the parent
field** before it is sent (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:196-215`: `parent_id in
local_ticket_types` and `parent_type != "epic"` ⇒ the parent diff is dropped via
`suppressed_out`/`dropped_field_sink`). The child then lands as an under-defined leaf with
no hint that its defining context lives elsewhere. Alt-link self-heal was rejected as
echo-unsafe. We need an echo-safe breadcrumb comment pointing the Jira user at the nearest
ancestor that *is* visible in Jira, never re-ingested inbound.

## Approach

Emit the breadcrumb from the **outbound comment differ**, not the apply-time scalar
recorder `pass_io.record_parent_divergence` (see Scope for why that seam is wrong).
Integrate it into `outbound_comments._diff_comments` (`outbound_comments.py:385`), which
already (a) resolves the child's full Jira comment list `jira_comments` (from the
snapshot, or one bounded `client.get_comments` live fetch when the snapshot lacks the
`comment` field — bug-4292 invariant), (b) builds the marker-stripped `jira_bodies` dedup
set, (c) holds `binding_store` and the `TicketTransport` `client`. Reusing the resolved
`jira_comments` avoids a second fetch.

On a bound child whose direct parent is type-collapsed (the suppression above), walk the
chain upward and name the **nearest ancestor with a bound Jira key** (`binding_store.get_jira_key`). Build the body via `_decorate_outbound_comment`
(`outbound_comments.py:209`, appends `RECONCILER_MARKER`) and return it as an ordinary
`{"action":"add",...}` mutation appended to `_diff_comments`' result, posted through the
existing path (`dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_dispatch_comments:347` →
`client.add_comment`, implemented by both backends: `adapters/jira/backend.py:361`,
`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:558`).

**Echo-safety (corrected).** The breadcrumb *is* mirrored outbound, so it must NOT be
caught by `_is_machine_marker_comment` (`outbound_comments.py:375-382`) — that matches
only `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` (`'BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:'`, `'Still stale as of'`) and
would *exclude* a comment from being sent; the body starts with neither prefix. Inbound
echo-safety comes solely from the `RECONCILER_MARKER` substring check in
`inbound_collection_diffs._diff_comments_inbound` (`inbound_collection_diffs.py:154`: `if
RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text: continue`). `_normalize_comment_body`
(`outbound_comments.py:184-206`) **strips** `RECONCILER_MARKER`, so the marker never makes
`_is_machine_marker_comment` fire and never enters the dedup key — it serves only the
inbound suppression at line 154.**Append-once / supersede.** Dedup on a **stable identity tag**
(`<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->`), not the variable ancestor key: before appending,
scan the resolved `jira_comments` (normalized via `_normalize_comment_body`, which does
not strip this tag) for the tag; if present, emit nothing. This is append-once AND robust
to cross-pass staleness — if the nearest represented ancestor later changes, a breadcrumb
is still detected so no conflicting second one is appended (first-writer-wins). The
outbound comment path is ADD-only (no transport-portable edit/delete), so the original is
intentionally not rewritten (accepted limitation below). Adds no transport capability,
cannot loop.

## Scope

- `outbound_comments.py` — add pure `_build_parent_breadcrumb(...)` and integrate it into
  `_diff_comments` (`:385`): after `jira_bodies` is built, when the drift condition holds
  and no resolved comment carries the tag, append one decorated `"add"`. New
  `_diff_comments` params `local_parents` (`{id->parent_id}`) and `local_ticket_types`,
  both defaulting to `None` (no breadcrumb when absent — every existing caller/test
  unchanged).
- `outbound_mutation_builders.py` — in `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` (`:163`), pass
  the new `local_parents` (threaded from the caller) and the already-in-scope
  `local_ticket_types` into the `_diff_comments(...)` call (`:277`).
- `outbound_differ.py` — in `compute_outbound_mutations` (`:449`), build `local_parents`
  `{t["ticket_id"]: t.get("parent_id")}` beside the existing `local_ticket_types` build
  (`:551`) and thread it into `_compute_outbound_update_mutation`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_parent_breadcrumb.py` (new).

**Out of scope (with reason):** `pass_io.record_parent_divergence` (`pass_io.py:80`) and
its call sites `dispatch_one.py:558,569,579` and `acli_cli_ops.py:158` are NOT touched.
Its signature `(kind, key, local_id, parent, exc, repo_root)` is scalar-only — `parent`
is the *failed* key/CLEAR sentinel — with no ticket graph, binding store, comment client,
or snapshot; `acli_cli_ops.py:158` passes `local_id=None` (transport boundary), so it
structurally cannot supply the inputs. The differ seam detects the same drift class
earlier with all inputs present.

**UPDATE path only.** The breadcrumb needs the child's Jira issue to exist (to post +
dedupe), so it is emitted from the bound path; on the create pass the parent is dropped
at birth but there is no child key yet, and the breadcrumb follows next pass. CREATE is
untouched.

## Body content contract

Deterministic (no timestamps, so dedup is stable). Nearest ancestor `PROJ-42`:

```
This ticket's parent hierarchy could not be fully represented in Jira. Nearest tracked ancestor: PROJ-42. Full parent context is maintained in rebar.
<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->

<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->
```

If ≥1 intervening ancestor was skipped for lacking a bound key, insert `One or more
intervening parent levels are not represented in Jira.` before the last sentence. The
first line starts with no `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` value (mirrored outbound); the
trailing `RECONCILER_MARKER` guarantees inbound suppression.

## Accepted limitation

No supersede/edit of a stale breadcrumb: the path is ADD-only and no transport-portable
edit/delete exists, so a changed nearest ancestor leaves the original in place — still a
valid "context lives upward, see rebar" pointer, preferred over conflicting duplicates.

## Portability

In-process differ logic plus the existing `TicketTransport` comment port (`add_comment`/
`get_comments`), implemented by both backends. No CI-system dependency, no new binary,
filesystem assumption, or transport capability; runs identically across library/CLI/MCP
and both Jira deployments. With `local_parents`/`local_ticket_types` absent it is a no-op.

## Testing / Acceptance Criteria

In-process unit tests over `_build_parent_breadcrumb`/`_diff_comments` (stub binding store,
synthetic snapshots; pure logic):

- [ ] A bound child with a type-collapsed, bound parent appends exactly one breadcrumb
  naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key and carrying both the
  `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` tag and `RECONCILER_MARKER` — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_emitted`.
- [ ] Append-once via the stable tag, including when the nearest represented ancestor
  changes across passes (no conflicting second comment) — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_idempotent_and_supersede`.
- [ ] When the walk skips an unbound intervening ancestor to reach a bound one, the body
  names the bound ancestor and states the intervening levels are not represented —
  verified by `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_unrepresented_intervening_ancestor_noted`.
- [ ] No ancestor with a bound Jira key ⇒ no breadcrumb — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_omitted_when_no_bound_ancestor`.
- [ ] The breadcrumb body is suppressed inbound by `_diff_comments_inbound` (carries
  `RECONCILER_MARKER`) — verified by `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_echo_safe`.
